On Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 10:37 AM, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide a tightly redacted set today and the full policy artifact by tomorrow morning.

Adding a couple of implementation specifics for the record (so the CAIQ response can reference concrete controls):

- Runner lifecycle: ephemeral runners are provisioned in a transient GKE node pool with a TTL of 35 minutes by default. Provisioning is mediated by a cluster-side controller that enforces a namespace tag (runner:ephemeral=true). After TTL expiration a GC job removes the node and associated service account tokens are revoked via KMS rotation.

- Access & auth: runners use short-lived service tokens issued by our internal token broker (max lifetime 15 minutes). No long-lived credentials are embedded in runner images.

- Log redaction: our log pipeline (Fluentd -> secured GCS) applies a redaction filter that masks any env var named with the prefix REDWOOD_SECRET_ or any value matching the KMS ciphertext regex. Archived artifacts exported for assessors are run through a second pass redaction script that replaces all base64 blobs > 256 chars with <REDACTED-BLOB>. The attached spreadsheet maps the artifact types (build.log, coverage.report, container.image.manifest) to the redaction rule and owner.

- PR gating: we require at least one codeowner approval and passing CI status checks; merges are blocked by an org-level branch protection rule. The sample CSV includes the approval timestamps and the check names.

If the assessor needs evidence of token revocation (e.g., KMS audit event), we can pull a 24-hour slice but that requires a data extraction ticket (we can expedite).

Regards,
